title: Towards Dynamic Benchmarks for Autonomous Materials Discovery
experiments_summary: The authors implement a demonstration of the MADE (MAterials Discovery Environment) benchmark using two chemical systems: a binary metal oxide (Na-O) and a ternary intermetallic (Co-Nb-Sn). Two structure generators are evaluated: (1) Random, which generates structures by sampling compositions of up to 12 atoms distributed randomly among constituent elements, placing atoms uniformly in the unit cell with lattice parameters sampled from U(3,15) Å and angles from U(60,120) degrees; and (2) MatterGen, which uses a pretrained diffusion-based generative model conditioned on the chemical system with a guidance parameter of 2.0. Each generator is paired with two acquisition functions: (1) Random acquisition, which selects uniformly at random from generated candidates, and (2) Diversity acquisition, which selects the candidate with the maximum minimum Euclidean distance in normalized composition space to all previously observed structures. For each round, 8 candidates are generated before the acquisition function selects one for oracle evaluation. The oracle used is orb-v3-conservative-inf-omat from the ORB MLIP family, which computes formation energies after relaxing structures using the FIRE optimizer for up to 100 steps or until maximum atomic forces reach 0.01 eV/Å in ASE. Initial known structures (H0) for elemental end-members and other stable phases are retrieved from the Materials Project using mixed GGA/GGA+U functionals and their energies are recomputed with the oracle. A stability tolerance of ε=0.01 eV/atom relative to the convex hull is used to classify new structures as stable, and pymatgen StructureMatcher is used to verify structural novelty. Each policy is evaluated over a query budget of 20 structures, and results are compared across all four policy combinations (generator × acquisition function) on both chemical systems.
